Holovanivsk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kirovohrad Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Holovanivsk's Jewish community, numbering 456 in 1790, grew to comprise 85 percent of the town's population by 1887 and 4,320 people (more than half the town) by 1897, supporting six prayer houses and a private Jewish school by the early 20th century. Following a December 1917 pogrom, Jews organized a well-armed self-defense group that successfully operated for a year and a half before its defeat in August 1919, when a subsequent pogrom claimed about 200 victims. All of Holovanivsk's Jews were killed en masse between August 1941 and February 1942, following the July 1941 German and Romanian occupation. This cemetery, established in the early 19th century, holds about 200 preserved headstones; local residents have planted a garden in a section no longer in use.
